title: Dow Jones| Nasdaq | US Stock Market Today | Live: US stocks seesaw as bond yields rise and AI spending surges - The Economic Times
text:
Dow Jones Today | US Stock Market Live: US stocks pared earlier gains in volatile trading as rising bond yields and concerns over Big Tech’s surging AI spending tempered optimism from Amazon’s 12% jump following strong cloud revenue growth.

The strength in wages reported by the Labor Department on Friday was concentrated in the goods-producing industries. Job growth accelerated between March and May. The momentum, however, fizzled in June. Economists describe the labor market as being stuck in a "low hire, low fire" ‌state.

"To manage against the risk that high inflation could become entrenched, I would rather tighten policy incrementally as we gather more data on the path of inflation and employment," said regional Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari, referring to surging inflation that has remained above the Fed's target for more than five years.

Interest-rate uncertainty deepened after the Federal Reserve kept its benchmark rate unchanged. Chair Kevin Warsh’s comments and a largely benign inflation report prompted investors to raise the probability of another hold in September to 33%, up from about 18% a week earlier, according to CME’s FedWatch tool.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor index is still down over 20% in July, which would ‌mark its biggest monthly fall since the housing bubble burst in late 2008. Investors instead took notice of other sectors, as the S&P 500 equally weighted index is on track for its fourth-straight month of gains.

Nasdaq futures led Wall Street higher on Friday after Amazon shares surged 11% on strong cloud revenue growth, easing concerns about returns on artificial intelligence investments. Gains were tempered by a 7.8% premarket drop in Apple after the iPhone maker warned that supply constraints would weigh on growth.
